definitions.explanation: Poetry and verse considered together as a literary form, covering both Chinese-style poems and Japanese forms such as waka and haiku.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{若|わか}いころから{詩歌|しいか}に{親|した}しんできた。
examples.english: He has been familiar with poetry since his youth.

examples.japanese: この{雑誌|ざっし}は{現代|げんだい}の{詩歌|しいか}を{幅広|はばひろ}く{紹介|しょうかい}している。
examples.english: This magazine introduces a wide range of contemporary poetry.

notes:
A broad term covering poetry and verse as a whole, including {和歌|わか}, {俳句|はいく}, and Chinese-style poems. A somewhat formal, literary word. It may also be read かし.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {詩歌|しいか}を{詠|よ}む: to compose poetry
- {詩歌|しいか}に{親|した}しむ: to enjoy and become familiar with poetry
- {詩歌|しいか}{管弦|かんげん}: poetry and music (classical arts)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {詩|し}: poem; poetry — usually a single poem or modern free verse
- {歌|うた}: song; waka — in classical contexts refers to {和歌|わか}
